chain.label: Captain obtained incomplete preflight weather briefing
chain.trigger: The weather package contained no weather information for along the flight route. Further, no in-flight weather advisories, en route forecast, or adverse weather information was found in the package.

chain.label: Both pilots fatigued from acute sleep loss and early start
chain.trigger: both pilots' performance was likely impaired by fatigue that resulted from their significant acute sleep loss, early start time, and possible untreated sleep disorders

chain.label: FAA did not require CRM training or SOPs for Part 135 operators
chain.trigger: the failure of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to require crew resource management (CRM) training and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for 14 CFR Part 135 operators

chain.label: Flight encountered unforecast mesoscale convective system near destination
chain.trigger: the pilots' first indication that the weather would be worse than they expected was about 0924...when the AWOS recorded by the CVR indicated thunderstorms and rain

caused_by.evidence: the captain was not aware of the changing conditions because he did not obtain a more recent forecast before departure

chain.label: Poor crew coordination, nonsterile cockpit, and lack of checklist discipline
chain.trigger: the pilots' poor crew coordination and lack of cockpit discipline

caused_by.evidence: although fatigue might have degraded the pilots' performance on the day of the accident, it most likely was not the only factor affecting their performance

if, as a Part 135 operator, East Coast Jets had been required to develop SOPs and its pilots had been required to adhere to them, many of the deficiencies demonstrated by the pilots during the accident flight...might have been corrected
they repeatedly expressed impatience with ATC and the weather radar displays

chain.label: Captain did not conduct approach briefing or brief missed approach/committed-to-stop point
chain.trigger: in response to the first officer's calling for the approach briefing, the captain only replied, 'it's gonna be the ILS to three zero.'

caused_by.evidence: this atmosphere permitted inadequate briefing of the approach and monitoring of the current weather conditions

chain.label: Crew failed to monitor changing winds and did not detect the tailwind
chain.trigger: the CVR did not record either pilot verbally monitoring the wind information, which would have been displayed on each of the pilots' electronic horizontal situation indicators and FMS displays

caused_by.evidence: eroded the safety margins provided by the checklists, and degraded the pilots' attention
a well-briefed and coordinated flight crew should have realized that changing winds would be possible as a result of the weather conditions

chain.label: About 8-knot tailwind on runway 30
chain.trigger: the instantaneous wind 12 seconds before landing was 195° at 17 knots, which would have resulted in a 5.6-knot tailwind

caused_by.evidence: AWOS observations made surrounding the time of the accident indicated wind shifts from the north to the south and the south-southeast during the 10 minutes before the accident

chain.label: Wet ungrooved 5,500-ft runway with degraded braking friction
chain.trigger: at the accident ground speeds, the friction available on the wet runway was only about 20 to 30 percent of that available on a dry runway

caused_by.evidence: echoes on descent into OWA and in the immediate vicinity consistent with the presence of light to moderate rain at the surface at OWA

chain.label: Crew continued to land on runway 30 without arrival landing distance assessment or considering runway 12
chain.trigger: the accident flight crew did not conduct an arrival landing distance assessment...The captain could have reasonably opted to hold, divert, or attempt to land on runway 12 with a headwind.

caused_by.evidence: If the pilots had obtained current wind information, they would have been prepared for the possibility of landing on runway 12 with a headwind rather than landing on runway 30 with a tailwind
the captain's focus on completing the flight degraded his attention to the changing weather situation
prevented them from recognizing and fully evaluating alternatives to landing on a wet runway in changing weather conditions

chain.label: Captain delayed full lift-dump deployment ~7 seconds after touchdown
chain.trigger: he failed to immediately deploy the lift-dump system after touchdown in accordance with company procedures, which negatively affected the airplane's deceleration

caused_by.evidence: the airbrakes moved to the OPEN position about 4.1 seconds after touchdown, and the lift-dump system was engaged about 8.9 seconds after touchdown
the CVR recorded the sound of the airplane touching down at 0945:04 and, at 0945:07, a sound consistent with the airbrake handle moving to the OPEN position

chain.label: Insufficient deceleration; airplane unable to stop within remaining runway
chain.trigger: after touching down 1,128 feet from the runway 30 threshold, the airplane would have needed an additional 4,669 feet to stop, for a total landing distance of about 5,800 feet, which is 300 feet longer than the available landing distance

caused_by.evidence: Assuming an 8-knot tailwind, the landing distances were 3,792 and 4,928 feet, respectively
the effective braking coefficients based on 14 CFR 25.109(c) most closely represented the actual braking performance of the airplane during the landing on the wet, ungrooved runway
the total landing distance on runway 30...assuming that lift-dump deployment was coincident with the opening of the airbrakes, was 5,530 feet, or 30 feet past the runway end

chain.label: Captain decided to go around 17+ seconds into landing roll with insufficient runway remaining
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this accident was the captain's decision to attempt a go-around late in the landing roll with insufficient runway remaining

caused_by.evidence: fatigue might have especially degraded the captain's performance and decision-making abilities when he had to decide while under time pressure whether to continue the landing or initiate a go-around
If the captain had conducted an approach briefing that included a committed-to-stop point...he may not have decided to attempt a go-around late in the landing roll

at some point during the landing roll, the captain likely became concerned that the airplane would run off the runway end and had to decide whether it was preferable to overrun the runway or attempt a go-around

chain.label: Flaps fully retracted to 0 degrees instead of 15 degrees for go-around
chain.trigger: Postaccident examination of the flaps indicated that they were fully retracted (that is, set at 0°), not set to 15° as required for a go-around.

caused_by.evidence: the captain stated, 'flaps,' and, about the same time, the CVR recorded a sound consistent with increasing engine noise
this setting may reflect the confusion and lack of crew coordination that can follow from unprofessional compliance with use of nonstandard terminology

chain.label: Airplane lifted off past runway end unable to climb, rolled right to 50+ degrees
chain.trigger: the captain stated, 'here we go....not flyin'...not flyin'.'...The roll angle increased to 50° at the time that the alert was issued.

caused_by.evidence: the airplane ran off the runway end at 0945:29 and lifted off the ground at 0945:34, about 978 feet from the runway end
the airplane could not have rotated and lifted off before the runway end with the flaps set at either 15° or 0°

chain.label: Collision with ILS localizer antenna structure beyond runway end
chain.trigger: the airplane collided with the runway 30 localizer antenna support structure, which was about 1,000 feet from the runway end

caused_by.evidence: the airplane lifted off about 978 feet beyond the threshold and subsequently impacted the ILS localizer antenna about 5 feet agl

chain.label: Airplane impacted cornfield and was destroyed
chain.trigger: The airplane then continued to roll to the right and descend, impacting the ground...it eventually came to rest in a cornfield...about 2,136 feet from the runway end

caused_by.evidence: The airplane then continued to roll to the right and descend, impacting the ground.

chain.label: Two pilots and six passengers fatally injured
chain.trigger: The two pilots and six passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces.

caused_by.evidence: the captain, first officer, and all of the passengers died as a result of traumatic injuries to the head, neck, chest, and extremities
